# fortiappseccloud_waf_rewriting_requests

Configures rewriting requests for one FortiAppSec Cloud application using the static app endpoint `/waf/apps/{ep_id}/rewriting_requests`. Set `template = false` and provide `configs` to manage settings directly. Set `template = true` and omit `configs` to inherit this module from the application's attached WAF template.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_rewriting_requests` resource for an application endpoint. Template-level settings are managed by `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_rewriting_requests`.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_rewriting_requests" "example" {
  ep_id    = fortiappseccloud_waf_app.example.ep_id
  template = false

  configs {
    status               = true
    x_forwarded_for      = true
    identify_original_ip = true
    x_header             = "X-Forwarded-For"

    rule_list {
      item {
        name                = "rewrite-example"
        action              = "rewrite-header-advanced"
        host_filter         = true
        host_expression     = "^(example\\.com)$"
        header_status       = true
        insert_header_name  = "X-Terraform-Matrix"
        insert_header_value = "enabled"

        remove_header {
          item {
            header = "X-Old-Header"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Import

Import using the application `ep_id`:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_rewriting_requests.example application-endpoint-id
```

The first read after import hydrates all ownership wrappers when `template = false`.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
